mappedTags.description:en: A temple mountain set back in the trees at the base of Phnom Bakheng, in materials typical of the 10th century. A brick tower opening to the east and originally decorated with stucco moulding surmounts four diminishing tiers in laterite.

pictures.author: NeuCeu
pictures.observations: Entire500x667 east view inspected. Four diminishing laterite terraces, three taller lower tiers and a short upper tier; very steep narrow stair between solid cheeks and terrace pier masses; summit landing; one open east-facing rectangular shrine door, grey moulded jamb/lintel, orange-brown brick pilasters, layered eaves and a rough truncated crown. Foreground path, guardian and trees are external context.

pictures.author: Leon petrosyan
pictures.observations: Entire500x750 oblique stair/door picture inspected. Narrow stair segments with thick laterite cheeks and pier masses at terrace levels, exposed warm weathered brick, moulded grey stone door frame and brick pilasters, layered cornices and eroded crown partly obscured by foliage. Exact tread and relief inventory is not inferred.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Specific mapped Baksei Chamkrong: four diminishing laterite terraces, four steep stone stairs with solid cheeks and terrace pier masses, summit landing and the surviving east-facing brick shrine with a real open doorway, three blind recesses, corner pilasters, moulded stone jambs and lintel, layered eaves and an eroded truncated crown. Secondary dimensions, individual tread inventory and carving are picture-led approximations. External forest, path and surviving forecourt guardian sculpture are not authored.
